The evaluation criteria include co-attention fusion scores, object detection metrics, Natural Language Processing metrics for Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers, and overall Visual Question Answering accuracy, among other pertinent dimensions. By taking into account both response correctness and the efficiency of individual components, the study seeks to obtain a sophisticated view of the system's performance. Open-ended evaluation criteria allow for a comprehensive assessment because of the Visual Question Answering assignment's varied nature. The results show that the system can intelligently answer to questions regarding visual content and demonstrate its potential for a wide range of practical applications. The project is open-sourced, encouraging community involvement and collaboration to push the boundaries of multi-modal question answering systems even farther.

articleTitle: Eye Gaze Tracking Towards User Attention Analysis
abstract: Eye-tracking is a method that involves monitoring the position and movement of eyes that can help towards wide variety of applications including gaming, augmented reality, virtual reality, assistive technologies, human computer interface, marketing and medical diagnostic applications. The authors in this paper uses L2CS-Net, a novel gaze estimation architecture built on ResNet-50. The model, was validated on the MPII Gaze dataset through 5-fold cross-validation and exhibited consistent reduction in combined loss during training, showcasing its promising performance in accurate gaze estimation. The performance of the model was demonstrated for an application of profiling the attention of the user and monitoring the off-screen glances of the user while watching a video. Thus, demonstrating potential applications towards user attention detection in educational and marketing applications.

articleTitle: Broccoli Classifiers: CNN and AdaBoost Models for Differentiating Indian Varieties
abstract: This study looks at three main kinds of broccoli - Pusa KTS-1, Green Magic, and Calabrese. It uses a method called Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) along with AdaBoost ensemble methods to see how these different types grow in Indian farms. They used a set of 1500 carefully taken pictures to teach and test how well the model works. A new kind of computer program called CNN and another one named AdaBoost joined together to make a very good score. They were able to tell different types apart with 97.10% accuracy by looking closely at small changes in pictures. Table I shows the model's strong accuracy, recall, and F1 scores. This confirmed that it is reliable at correctly grouping each kind while catching many different examples from every category fairly. Figure 3 showed the new method was better than the old ways. So, it is at the top for classifying different types of broccoli. Beyond just farming, this study could lead to wider uses in automated sorting systems. These changes can affect how farmers grow and sell their crops. The success of the study shows how well machine learning models can make plant variety classification more accurate and automate it. In the future, the model can be improved by adding more data and making it better. This will lead to higher accuracy when using it on farms or with new tech gadgets. This study is a big step to change how computer systems classify types of vegetables. It brings important help in farming practices and making markets different from each other.

articleTitle: A Novel Machine Learning Approach to Detect Application Layer DDoS Attacks
abstract: Attackers use application-layer DDoS (App-DDoS) attacks, which aim to bring down the victim's server by sending fake packets in its direction. Because malicious packets mimic the behavior of legitimate users and contain real source IP addresses, neither attackers nor IDS can distinguish packets from legitimate users. Regardless of the kind, the primary objective of DDoS attackers is to make the victim servers react so slowly that they become unusable or shut down entirely. They overburden the victim server's bottleneck resources in order to do this. For application-layer DDoS attacks, CPU cycles, RAM, I/O bandwidth, disk bandwidth or database bandwidth and TCP/IP stacks are the intended bottleneck resources. Through the use of valid requests, the attacker overwhelms the bottleneck resources in App-DDoS attacks. An attacker overwhelms limited resources with real requests in App-DDoS attacks. Any bot that wants to participate in an attack must first establish a TCP connection to the victim's server, which requires a real IP address to perform such an attack. An App DDoS security technique's primary goal is to identify and separate malicious traffic from legal traffic. Because attackers intentionally generate App-DDoS traffic to mimic real traffic, this problem is challenging. However, experienced hackers are always evolving their toolkits and creating increasingly complex App DDoS attacks, making it harder to identify attack activity. On the other hand, the victim server can stop all traffic coming from the attack sources once the attacked traffic is identified. Over the past decade, a number of traditional, heuristic, and more recently, machine learning (ML)-based methods have been developed to identify and differentiate App-DDoS activity from real traffic. Previously used traditional strategies, such are heuristic and classic approaches, use traffic engineer-programmed rules to identify App DDoS activity. Due to the constantly changing and evolving nature of App-DDoS attacks, conventional methods have not been very effective in detecting App-DDoS traffic. CICIDS-2017 dataset contains different types of DDoS attacks such as slowloris, httptest, goldeneye, hulk. This study proposes a feature selection strategy to improve the speed and efficiency of a machine learning solution for detecting DDoS attacks, leading to a significant reduction in feature subsets and ensemble technique to detect AL-DDoS attacks.

articleTitle: Aspect Based Sentiment Analysis
abstract: Sentiment analysis is considered an effective tool that extracts the emotional state information of Human beings. The current researcher concentrates on aspect-based sentiment analysis as enables user to dictate the sentiments of an aspect in a specific context. Machine learning techniques are found to be a significant prospect in evaluating sentiments in online contexts. This review article provides the levels of sentiment analysis and its application. Then a brief A description of the sentiment analysis taxonomy is given in this article to abstract the structural pattern of the recent aspect-based sentiment analysis technique. The brief analysis of the datasets used, published journal, year of publication, performance Metrics, and achievement, helps the researchers to design an effective Aspect-based sentiment Analysis framework with high performance.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Team Personality Tourism Route Design Based on Fuzzy APACA
abstract: In order to solve the challenge of multi-objective team personalized tourism route design, in view of the shortcomings of the existing divide and conquer algorithms, this study proposes an innovative personalized tourism route design method based on fuzzy APACA. This new scheme uses the principles of gradient descent theory to accurately identify and locate key influencing factors, and accordingly carries out a sensible classification of indicators to reduce possible interference. At the same time, by using the unique mechanism of fuzzy APACA, this scheme cleverly constructs the design strategy of tourism routes. The empirical results show that this scheme shows a significant improvement compared with the traditional divide and conquer algorithm in terms of key performance indicators such as the accuracy of personalized tourism route design and the processing efficiency of key factors, showing its obvious strong advantages. In the multi-objective team, the personalized tourism route design plays a crucial role, which can accurately predict and optimize the growth trend and output results of the multi-objective team's personalized tourism route design. However, in the face of complex simulation tasks, traditional divide-and-conquer algorithms show some inherent shortcomings, especially when dealing with multi-level challenges, their performance is often unsatisfactory. To overcome this, this study introduces a new idea of fuzzy APACA optimization for the design of personalized tourism routes, and accurately controls the influencing parameters through gradient descent theory, which is used as the road map for index allocation, and then uses fuzzy APACA to innovate and construct a system scheme. The test results clearly point out that in the context of the evaluation criteria, the new scheme has been significantly optimized in terms of accuracy and processing speed for a variety of challenges, showing stronger performance superiority. Therefore, in the design of multi-objective team personalized tourism routes, the simulation scheme based on fuzzy APACA successfully overcomes the shortcomings of the traditional divide and conquer algorithm, and significantly improves the accuracy and operation efficiency of the simulation.

articleTitle: Multi-Disease Prediction and Classifier: A Comprehensive Approach for Healthcare Decision Support
abstract: The speedy identification and early detection of diseases that are deadly are greatly important when it comes to human life saving. On the other hand, the existence of poor medical system alongside the lack of equal distribution of healthcare presents a barrier towards early disease detection leaving death as the only option. One of the ways to tackle these problems is the utilization of machine learning in detection and analysis of diseases risk is machine learning promising. Utilizing predictive analytics in medicine, practitioners can make accurate and relevant medical insights promptly, relying on the information they have. The work focused on generating prediction models to identify seven most severe illnesses: diabetes, pneumonia, malaria, heart disease, kidney disease, breast cancer, and liver disease, using an algorithm of Random Forest Classifier. Alongside this, the Convolutional Neural Networks were utilized for the detection of malaria and pneumonia. Users can get better knowledge about their health problems and at the same time reduce the access constraints to healthcare by using machine learning. This research is also about designing a web app with the Flask framework and will give its consumers an easy-to-use tool for the simultaneous prediction of all seven diseases. Such a user interface grants better healthcare access and results in the use of proactive measures, as people can take a more active role in their wellness.

articleTitle: Audio Deepfakes: Feature Extraction and Model Evaluation for Detection
abstract: Cutting-edge AI-driven tools are currently employed for replicating human voices, leading to the emergence of audio deepfakes. Initially designed to enhance experiences like audio-books, the potential misuse of audio deepfakes poses significant risks to public safety. Despite advancements in detecting video deepfakes, identifying audio deepfakes remains challenging. We employ methods to extract features such as Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients, chromagrams, spectral contrast, tonnetz, and Mel-spectrograms from audio samples. The extracted deep features are concatenated together and then employed in machine learning and deep learning models to evaluate the ASVspoof2021 dataset to categorize it into bonafide and spoofed speech utterances. The experimental results reveal that the multilayer perceptron model achieves the highest accuracy rate of 96.073%, while SVM, k-NN, XGBoost, and RF produce accuracy rates of 93.58%, 94.58%, 93.544%, and 93.58%, respectively. Additionally, DL models, including CNN, achieve an accuracy rate of 98.2%, DNN of 97.6%, and LSTM of 97.7%, showcasing the superiority of CNN in identifying deepfake audio amidst the evolving landscape of synthetic media.

articleTitle: Ethnicity Prediction From Audio Samples for Different Languages Using Convolutional Neural
abstract: “Ethnicity Prediction from Voice Samples” deals with prediction of a person's ethnicity from his/her voice samples. Ethnicity Prediction has gained more and more importance and attention in fields like security, recommendations systems, learning apps etc. The proposed work uses a customized Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) based model to predict the ethnicity of the speaker based on combination of varied audio features like Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC), pitch, energy, and zero crossing rate. The different voice samples are obtained from the popular Speech Accent Archive Dataset. Augmentation of data by performing time and pitch shifting proved to give a significant boost in the accuracy as it increased the number of voice recordings. The work also compares the performance of the proposed model with other state-of-art models like LSTM. The F-score obtained was 98% for the class Russian, Polish and 90% for the class French, Italian, Spanish i.e. Romance Languages and 80% for mixed language category that comprises of Indian, Italian, German and Polish.

articleTitle: Automated Verification of Open/Closed Principle: A Code Analysis Approach
abstract: The SOLID principles are foundational to software engineering, focusing on the maintainability, scalability, and extensibility of software systems. The Open/Closed Principle (OCP), a pivotal element among these principles, underscores the need to design software modules that are open for extension yet closed for modification. This research explores automated verification techniques for OCP, addressing the validation of software modules through extensibility and adaptability assessments. The principal objectives involve the development of a code analysis approach and a methodology capable of automating the verification of adherence to OCP in developed codes, providing actionable insights to software developers. The system focuses on specific aspects of OCP, including inheritance, abstraction, and polymorphism, and aims to provide clear indications of where violations occur within a codebase. The implementation uses the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) analysis to examine class definitions. The automated analysis of Python code using the defined rules offers a clear understanding of OCP adherence. Results are presented in Pandas DataFrames, indicating potential violations and providing developers with actionable insights to enhance code quality and maintainability. Overall, the automated code verification system aims to enhance code quality and adherence to fundamental design principles, paving the way for advancements in automated code analysis and software engineering practices.

articleTitle: Enhancing Liver Tumor Segmentation Using UNET++ with Attention Architecture
abstract: Medical image segmentation is crucial for analyzing specific structures or abnormalities in diagnostic images, playing a pivotal role in enhancing accuracy and efficiency in medical diagnostics and treatment planning. The number of cases involving liver tumors is steadily rising, therefore it's critical to develop a technique to automate the diagnostic and treatment planning process in order to improve accuracy and lessen the burden on doctors. Medical image segmentation plays a critical role in improving diagnostics and therapies for accurate illness identification, customized medicine, treatment planning, and cost-effective healthcare. Liver tumor segmentation is an essential first step in the early detection, planning, and identification of liver tumors. Due to the labor-intensive manual nature of the profession and the need for a solid understanding of human anatomy, the doctors are overworked. A technique for automatically classifying liver tumors is capable of efficiently and accurately handling massive amounts of data. This will allow physicians to concentrate on other crucial responsibilities like clinical decision-making, patient involvement, and treatment planning. The Unet++ with attention, our proposed architecture, outshines both counterparts Unet and Unet++ with remarkable IOU and DICE scores of 0.96 and 0.97, respectively, coupled with a perfect accuracy of 1.0. This highlights the effectiveness of incorporating attention mechanisms, showcasing our model as a superior choice for tasks demanding precise segmentation.

articleTitle: Dynamic Framework for Optimized Cloud Service Selection Using Adaptive Weighting and Enhanced TOPSIS
abstract: As cloud services become increasingly integral to business and technology landscapes, effective selection and composition of these services are paramount. This paper introduces a novel framework that significantly enhances the cloud service selection process by incorporating an advanced Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) algorithm. The proposed framework uniquely adapts to real-time user preferences and market trends through a dynamic weighting system, thereby refining decision-making accuracy. Comparative scenario-based testing shows an 88% improvement in decision accuracy over existing methods. Additionally, the modified TOPSIS algorithm achieves execution time reductions between 12<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> and 45%, outperforming standard benchmarks. This framework is further distinguished by a dynamic weighting mechanism tailored to user feedback, which has resulted in high user satisfaction, averaging 4.2 out of 5. Comprehensive evaluation criteria within the framework ensure a thorough assessment of cloud service suitability, establishing a robust, adaptive, and user-centric approach to navigating the complex cloud service landscape.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Hausdorff Distance Algorithm Automated Test Platform
abstract: In view of the limitations of the traditional DFS algorithm in the conception and execution of an automated testing framework, a design and implementation scheme of the automated test platform based on the Hausdorff distance algorithm was proposed. Firstly, the influencing factors is accurately located through the measurement distance theory, and the indicators is reasonably divided to reduce interference, and the design and implementation scheme of the automated test platform is constructed by using the Hausdorff distance algorithm. Experimental results show that the proposed scheme is superior to the traditional DFS algorithm in terms of the design and implementation accuracy of the automated test platform and the processing time of influencing factors under certain evaluation criteria, and has obvious advantages. The conception and execution of an automated testing framework plays an extremely important role in the automated production line platform, which can accurately predict and optimize the growth characteristics and product generation of the automated production line platform. However, the traditional DFS algorithm has certain limitations in solving the simulation problem of the test platform, especially when dealing with complex problems. In this paper, the design and implementation scheme of an automated test platform based on Hausdorff distance algorithm is proposed to better solve this problem. In this scheme, the influencing factors is accurately located through the measurement distance theory, so as to determine the division of indicators, and the Hausdorff distance algorithm is used to construct the scheme. Experimental results show that under certain evaluation criteria, the accuracy and speed of the scheme is significantly improved for different problems, and it has better performance. Therefore, the simulation scheme based on Hausdorff distance algorithm can better solve the limitations of the traditional DFS algorithm and improve the simulation accuracy and efficiency in the conception and execution of an automated testing framework.

articleTitle: Enhancing Cucumber Leaf Disease Severity Prediction through Convolutional Neural Networks and Random Forest Integration
abstract: The abstract functions as a succinct summary of the main conclusions drawn from the study. By utilizing the extensive classification performance metrics shown in the attached table, the abstract highlights the accuracy and efficiency of the model in predicting the various severity levels of Cucumber Mosaic Virus (CMV) infections on cucumber leaves. The model is very good at defining CMV infection levels; the precision, recall, or F1-score metrics show this clearly, with values that are consistently high for all severity levels. Furthermore, the support values provide insightful information about the distribution of the dataset by highlighting the frequency of occurrences for each severity level. The model demonstrated an outstanding 97.59% overall accuracy on a dataset consisting of 4908 photos of cucumber leaves. The Support Proportion boundary further emphasizes how different severity categories are represented within the dataset, which improves the comprehension of the makeup of the data. Additionally, It has been known that the overall accuracy rate is not good, which indicates that many people get it wrong. However, if they look at a weighted average level, they can see that it is quite effective in predicting disease severity caused by CMV. This astute finding not only shows the effectiveness of the recommended methodology but also implies interesting applications in agricultural areas. When diseases become severe, the model has significant potential to provide valuable insights for timely interventions and strategic management methods. Cucumber production will then realize the protection of crop productive yield and improved product quality under the pressure of CMV infection.

articleTitle: SPARROW: Smart Precision Agriculture Robot for Ridding of Weeds
abstract: The advancements in precision agriculture are vi-tal to support the increasing demand for global food supply. Precision spot spraying is a major step towards reducing chemicalusage for pest and weed control in agriculture. A novel spot spraying algorithm that autonomously detects weeds and performs trajectory planning for the sprayer nozzle has been proposed. Furthermore, this research introduces a vision-based autonomous navigation system that operates through the detected crop row, effectively synchronizing with an autonomous spraying algorithm. This proposed system is characterized by its cost effectiveness that enable the autonomous spraying of herbicides onto detected weeds.

articleTitle: Agriculture Advances: Federated Learning CNN's for Combatting Banana Leaf Diseases
abstract: The study combines federated learning with convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to solve a ubiquitous issue-the banana leaf diseases that dramatically affect global agricultural output. The study focuses on five customary nasal illnesses that consumers suffer, which are modelable and provide analytic information while protecting their data from an attacker. In a federated learning setting, each model is trained using data specific to the client. These parameters are then fine-tuned to create a robust global model. Each client's on-site data (kx_1 to kx_5) is specifically examined to determine accuracy, recall, and Fl-score assessment. Then, all the results are combined to reach the aggregate using federated averaging methods. Micro, macro, and weighted average precisions are determined to put together four performance measures that consider class imbalance and classify whole results more comprehensively. Our results show that the diseases are being classified with high accuracy, which is a significant factor in diagnosis. For keyword x _1, the macro average precision achieved 94.84%, which increased to 96.32% for keyword x_5; the weighted average accuracy went up from 94.3% to 96.32%. Micro-average precision reached 96.32%, compared to 94.82 % in the previous one. It is highest in the case of kx_5. This demonstrates the model's ability to get the correct knowledge from multiple data resources. The findings show federated learning is a solution that fits well to agricultural situations and is capable enough to bring a breakthrough for plant disease detection by being a scalable, efficient, and privacy-aware solution for a global agricultural problem.

articleTitle: Enhancing Nutrition Tracking: Webcam-Based Fruit and Vegetable Recognition and Calorie Measurement Using Image Processing and Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: The “Enhancing Nutrition Tracking” wander epitomizes a groundbreaking agreeable vitality between fake bits of knowledge (AI) and food science. Through the utilization of Convenient Net convolutional neural frameworks, this creative system passes on realtime normal item affirmation and correct calorie estimations, in this way empowering clients to make taught dietary choices. Central to its value is the visual emphasis on carbohydrate substance, ensuring clients have a comprehensive understanding of their food choices and dietary intake. This project's trademark lies in its user-friendly interface, arranged to streamline the strategy of capturing characteristic item and vegetable pictures for incite dietary bits of information. By reliably joining AI advancement into conventional assignments, individuals can effortlessly get to basic wholesome information, empowering more advantageous eating affinities and way of life choices. Besides, continuous ask almost endeavors search for to refine the system's realtime characteristic item recognizable confirmation capabilities and examine the immersive potential of virtual reality for in-depth wholesome assessments. By initiating the integration of AI and virtual reality advancements, the “Enhancing Nutrition Tracking” amplify focuses to catalyze a worldview move in food watching.

articleTitle: Attack Detection in Industrial IoT via Deep Hybrid Model on Solving Class Imbalance Problem
abstract: The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) emerged as an acceptable data processing architecture as several sectors have gone digital. Nevertheless, there are still difficult problems with IIoT, such as the reliability of 3rd parties, data authenticity, effectiveness 'as well as system reliability. This paper proposes a deep hybrid model based industrial IoT Attack Detection (DHM-IIoTAD) by following four steps like preprocessing, feature extraction, attack detection, & mitigation. Moreover, the pre processing is the initial step to solve the class imbalance problem. Then, the features including Correlation based feature, and higher order statistical based features are extracted during the feature extraction phase. Further, the deep hybrid model combining the models like Deep maxout & Bi- LSTM model is utilized during the attack detection stage, which determines the final detection outcome with Improved Score level fusion. After the detection process, the mitigation is performed via entropy-based mitigation process. Finally, the performance of DHM-IIoTAD scheme is compared over extant models based on certain metrics including FNR, sensitivity, NPV, accuracy, FPR, precision, specificity, MCC, and F-measure, respectively for WUSTL-IIOT-2018 Dataset and IoT Intrusion Dataset.

articleTitle: Optimized Plant Species Classification through MobileNet-Enhanced Hybrid Models
abstract: Medicinal plants are used to cure various diseases such as asthma, cancer, heart disease etc. Plant identification plays a pivotal role in various domains such as agriculture, ecology, and environmental conservation. Manual identification of plant species is tedious and time consuming as there exist inter class similarity and intra class variations among the plant species that may lead to human error. Hence automatic identification is required based on machine learning and deep learning models. In this study, we propose two novel hybrid models for accurate plant species classification, leveraging the combination of deep learning architectures. The first hybrid model integrates InceptionNetV3 and MobileNet, achieving an accuracy of 88.11 %, while the second hybrid model combines AlexNet and MobileNet, outperforming the first model with an accuracy of 93.86 %. Both hybrid models employ deep learning classifiers. This research underscores the efficacy of hybrid models in enhancing plant species classification accuracy and contributes towards advancing the plant identification. The experiments are carried out using self-built datasets that are captured in unconstrained environment

articleTitle: Novel AI Multimodal Approach for Combating Against Pulmonary Carcinoma
abstract: Lung cancer exhibits a significantly higher prevalence and fatality rate in comparison to other prevalent malignancies on a global scale. Prompt identification of worrisome lung cyst is crucial in the battle against lung cancer. The increasing accessibility of clinical data, such as low-dose computed tomography (LDCT), histology entire slide images, electronic health records, and sensor signals from medical Internet of Things (IoT) devices, has elevated the significance of artificial intelligence technologies in the management of pulmonary carcinoma. This survey offers a comprehensive examination of the existing and emerging artificial intelligence techniques utilized in the battle against lung malignancies. We explore innovative artificial intelligence techniques for the detection and diagnosis of lung nodules in CT scans, in addition to the commonly used deep learning models. Federated deep learning models are specifically engineered to leverage data from several centers while giving utmost importance to privacy and confidentiality. Multi-modal deep learning models seek to integrate clinical and visual data from diverse sources. Additionally Developers create interpretable deep learning models to offer clinicians a clear understanding of the model's internal mechanisms. Furthermore, it will aid clinicians in improving their comprehension of the developing AI technology.

articleTitle: Efficient Feature Extraction for Classification of Alzheimer's Abnormalities Using Deep Learning
abstract: Recent machine learning AD predictions employed feature selection and extraction methods. The literature research revealed several attempts to identify AD by using different Deep learning layer and micro-simulation techniques. However, identifying important features that can detect AD extremely early remains a difficult task. Automation, poor classification accuracy, over fitting, etc. are the other challenges while using machine learning algorithms. The recent progression of using deep learning methods has received the significant attention for the automatic AD classification. CNN's strategy, while successful, has certain drawbacks: (1) The CNN model uses local receptive fields, shares weights, and subsamples, (2) deep neural networks need a lot of labeled sample training models to avoid over fitting, which may cause the loss of crucial information like representative features at various frequencies and orientations; and (3) the higher computational overhead is another challenge. Therefore, these challenges motivate us the need of the proposed study. The scope of the proposed study is limited to the classification of AD from the input medical images.

articleTitle: Federated Learning-Based Flood Forecasting Model Enhancing Predictive Accuracy and Privacy in Flood Prediction
abstract: Flooding is a common natural disaster that significantly impacts property, crops, the economy, and human lives. Researchers have long struggled with flood prediction due to the challenges of data privacy, availability, and security. This paper proposes a flood forecasting model using federated learning, a modern AI innovation that ensures data privacy, availability, and security. The model combines locally trained models of 18 customers, determines the flood station, and provides a five-day flood alarm for a specific client. A nearby feed forward brain organization (FFNN) model is prepared at the client station, using regional factors like snow liquefying, precipitation spillover, stream directing, and hydrodynamics to predict the predicted water level. The model has 84<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> accuracy in predicting past floods in the selected zone between 2010 and 2015. The authors also use cutting-edge algorithms like Convolution2D Neural Network, which have a successful prediction accuracy of over 90%. The authors have extended CNN2D for flood forecasting to increase accuracy.

articleTitle: Vision-Based Solutions for Human Activity Recognition across Course and Fine Levels
abstract: This paper focuses on detection of human activities both at course level and finer levels. A course level activity like squats and finer level activity like hand gestures were detected using computer vision techniques and machine learning algorithms. The study integrates state-of-the-art technologies such as Media Pipe to detect pose landmarks and recognize hand gestures in real time. In squat analysis, an angle between pose landmark and real time pose was determined that enabled assessment of correctness of the squats. While for hand gesture recognition, a custom model training on a dataset with noisy backgrounds was done and validation accuracy of 70% was obtained. Despite the lower initial accuracy, the approach ensures improved robustness in practical applications. As a case study, the gesture recognition system was deployed for applications including scrolling of the screen, changing the slides of presentation.

articleTitle: Implementing CNN and RF Models for Multi-Level Classification: Deciphering Beetroot Aphid Disease Severity
abstract: Beetroot aphid infestation is one of the most serious threats to agricultural yield and food security. In this study, we hope to use machine learning models based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Random Forest (RF), among others, that can accurately classify the three different severity levels of beetroot aphid disease. A complete dataset was assembled, containing 14,000 images across six levels of severity, and carefully preprocessed for network training. The developed models achieved outstanding results, with an overall accuracy of 97.92 % in identifying levels of severity. The CNN, an image classification expert itself, distinguished very accurately and precisely the complex patterns in these images. Meanwhile, the RF model, using feature extraction techniques, was very accurate and there were differences between levels of severity. By comparing these models, the relative performance subtleties and possible practical applications can be seen. Both models show very high levels of accuracy, but issues resulting from practical considerations suggest that CNN should be used in scenarios where it is important to have visual clues. Meanwhile, assuming limited resources, RF may play a bigger role. These study results greatly facilitate applications of precision agriculture since they create common tools that can be used to make more timely and accurate evaluations of disease severity--information that is essential for effective crop protection plans and operations.

articleTitle: Precision in Plant Pathology: A Hybrid Model Approach for BYDV Syndrome Degrees
abstract: Barley Yellow Dwarf Disorder (BYDV) is a big danger to grains, so we need better ways for early finding and the right grouping. This study answers this important question by introducing a new mixed model. It helps combine the best parts of convolutional neural networks (CNN) and naive Bayes algorithms to make smart decisions. The main goal is to classify how bad BYDV sickness is in three categories. This step will help put control measures and reduce the loss of crops into effect. The start of the model's plan comes from a very carefully chosen set of 8600 high-quality pictures showing barley plants with BYDV disease. These came together to make up its data until they were ready for use. In this data set, our mix of models does very well with an overall correct rate that could be as high as 97.30%. It is useful for seeing how different diseases show up. Going beyond simple correctness, exact performance measures like accuracy, precision, and recall give a detailed assessment of how well the model can make decisions between things. This big look shows how good the model is at reducing both wrongly saying something matters and not recognizing it enough in all levels of BYDV sickness. This three-way check helps us to know more about the model's skills in dealing with the hard job of separating BYDV into different groups. Additionally, by comparing our mixed method model with what already exists in books and research articles we gain insight into its unique benefits.

articleTitle: TreeIDNet: Species Identification through Video Analysis using Detectron2-Based Computer Vision
abstract: Tree species identification plays a crucial role in various environmental monitoring and conservation efforts. In this paper, we present TreeIDNet, a system for species identification through video analysis using Detectron2-based computer vision techniques. The proposed system leverages the capabilities of the Detectron2 framework, for instance segmentation and object detection tasks. We begin by collecting a dataset of video footage containing diverse tree species, annotated with bounding boxes for training purposes. The training pipeline involves custom data augmentation techniques, model training, and evaluation to ensure accurate species identification. Once trained, TreeIDNet can detect and identify tree species in video frames, enabling real-time or batch processing for environmental surveillance applications. We evaluate the system's performance on a separate validation dataset and demonstrate its effectiveness in accurately identifying tree species. Our model can play a pivotal role in environmental monitoring and conservation by swiftly and accurately identifying tree species, crucial for biodiversity conservation, forest management, environmental monitoring, research, and education. Its efficiency and scalability make it a valuable tool for addressing pressing environmental challenges. The deployment of TreeIDNet has the potential to streamline species identification processes, leading to more efficient and informed decision-making in conservation efforts. Additionally, its versatility allows for seamless integration into existing environmental monitoring systems, enhancing their capabilities for long-term sustainability and ecosystem preservation.

articleTitle: Research on the Quality Detection Method of Camellia Oleifera Seed Based on Neural Network
abstract: In order to detect the water content of Camellia oleifera seeds quickly and accurately, and also to solve the problems of time-consuming and labor-intensive methods of traditional drying and detection methods, this paper proposes a non-destructive test method for water content of Camellia oleifera seeds based on hyperspectral technology. This paper takes Camellia oleifera seeds as the research object, determines the water content of Camellia oleifera seeds, and establishes a spectral model. The Camellia oleifera seed spectrum was pre-processed with SG convolution smoothing, first-order differential, second-order differential, and multiple scattering correction (MSC), and effective sensitivity wavelengths were extracted through stepwise regression. Partial least squares regression (PLSR), BP neural network, and A radial basis (RBF) neural network method is used to establish prediction models, externally verify the models, and select the optimal prediction model. It is shown that the spectrally sensitive bands with high correlation coefficients are 410 ~ 450nm, 610 ~620nm, 780 ~ 880nm and 940 ~ 971nm. The correlation coefficient of the correction set of the partial least squares regression model established is 0.9534, the root mean square error of the correction set is 0.22 after preprocessing using multiple scattering correction (MSC), the correlation coefficient of the verification set is 0.9399, and the root mean square error of the verification set is 0.27, which are better than BP neural network model and RBF neural network model. The use of hyperspectral technology to detect the water content of Camellia oleifera seeds is feasible, and it can provide an effective basis for the non-destructive online detection of water content of Camellia oleifera seeds.

articleTitle: Real Time Object Detection using Markov Random Fields: Video Anomaly Detection
abstract: This research focuses on the field of video anomaly detection, using the combined strength of the Markov Random Fields (MRFs) and autoencoder systems. The image-segmentation model proposed is based on the use of MRF, which is being used its spatial-temporal abilities to, for one, improve its ability to differentiate abnormalities in video content. The use of MRFs and autoencoders for the integration of the MRFs and autoencoders forms a comprehensive representation of the video data, improving the detection of abnormal activities. A wide range of testing is performed on videos randomly selected from the AVENUE dataset in order to emphasize the effectiveness of the proposed method, which outperforms other approaches. In particular, the approach significantly reduces the computation time of the anomaly detection by 60% when compared to the conventional frame extraction method. This efficiency improvement is an indication of the feasibility of this model in detecting anomalies in practical surveillance applications and has the required attributes that can be used to detect an anomaly in the surveillance system within a short time. The results reveal the potential benefits of the proposed framework for the improvement of the anomaly detection accuracy and operational effectiveness, adding to its practical viability being deployed in surveillance settings.

articleTitle: Integrated Framework for Enhanced Carrot Disease Classification: CNN and Random Forest Integration
abstract: The purpose of this research is to construct a classification model that is both reliable and accurate by using the most advanced machine learning methods available for detecting illnesses that damage carrots. Through the use of Convolutional Neural Networks (also known as CNNs) as well as Random Forest techniques, the model demonstrates remarkable effectiveness in identifying a collection of illnesses that are connected with carrots. Outstanding accuracy rates, ranging from 92.65% to 95.04%, are highlighted by the assessment measures, which are applied to a variety of diseases, including Black Root Rot, Cavity Spot, Common Scab, Sclerotinia Rot - White Mold, as well as Lateral Root Dieback. The ability of the algorithm to dependably retrieve relevant samples under a variety of sickness categories is an exceptionally intriguing aspect of the approach. The simple fact that the memory scores run from 92.31% to 95.17% shows that this is a real skill. These three averages-the macro, the weighted, and the micro-are very important because they show that the method works well and reliably to group diseases over time. This is how they choose to act because it shows that the plan is working. The data shows that the mean (weighted) value is about 94.14%, the micro average value is about 94.85%, and the macro median value is about 94.12%. It can be seen from these numbers that the system stays stable when measuring it in different ways. The weighted mean is 94.14%, and the micro average is 94.85% in this case. According to the results of this thorough evaluation, the program is capable of accurately identifying and classifying a wide range of diseases that are linked to carrots. Just the fact that the model can do this shows that it is possible. Not only does this model have important effects for study, but it could also be used to test things automatically. Because of this feature, finding diseases in carrot areas would be easier and better. The way that study is done changes because of this idea.

articleTitle: Multifaceted Discrete Emotion Recognition from EEG Physiological Signals via Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: Emotions, intricate mental states shaped by neu-rophysiological alterations influenced by cognitive processes, sensory inputs, behaviours, and diverse experiences, remain a compelling domain for exploration. The Electroencephalogram (EEG) is a potent tool that directly quantifies these emotional variations by capturing brain signals. Recent strides in emotion recognition have harnessed traditional machine learning classifiers to automate the identification of human emotions with remarkable success. This paper delves into the relatively underexplored Discrete Emotion Model, unveiling its capacity to achieve outstanding accuracy despite historical reservations regarding its effectiveness, using the ECSMP (Emotion, Cognition, Sleep, and Multi-model Physiological signals) dataset. It has two distinct environments, Video watching, and CANTAB-based cognitive assessment phases, enabling seamless data collection and analysis. This research effectively quantifies emotion for binary classification (classifies the type of emotion felt) and multiclass classification (classifies the intensity of emotion felt), elevating emotion recognition capabilities through the synergy of EEG technology. The exceptional performance of XGBoost, with a 96.5% accuracy rate in binary classification and 95% in multiclass emotion recognition, highlights its prowess compared to the other models tested.

articleTitle: Abnormal Event Monitoring and Alarm Optimization of Power System Based on Improved Genetic Algorithm
abstract: In order to solve the challenges of abnormal event monitoring and alarm optimization in power system, in view of the shortcomings of the existing improved particle swarm algorithm, an innovative abnormal event monitoring and alarm optimization method based on improved genetic algorithm is proposed. This new approach leverages the principles of best practice for group foraging to precisely identify and locate key influencing factors, and accordingly intelligently classify indicators to reduce possible interference. At the same time, using the unique mechanism of improved genetic algorithm, this scheme cleverly constructs a design strategy for systematic abnormal event monitoring. The empirical results show that the proposed scheme shows a significant improvement comprised with the traditional improved particle swarm optimization in key performance indicators such as the accuracy of abnormal event monitoring and alarm optimization, and the processing efficiency of key factors, showing its obvious strong advantages. In the power system, abnormal event monitoring and alarm optimization plays a vital role, which can accurately predict and optimize the growth trend and output results of abnormal event monitoring and alarm optimization in the power system. However, in the face of complex simulation tasks, traditional improved particle swarm algorithms show some inherent shortcomings, especially when dealing with multi-level challenges, their performance is often unsatisfactory. To overcome this, this study introduces a new idea of abnormal event monitoring and alarm optimization with improved genetic algorithm optimization, and accurately controls the influencing parameters through the optimal theory of group foraging, and uses it as a road map for index allocation, and then uses the improved genetic algorithm to innovate and construct a system scheme. The test results clearly point out that in the context of the evaluation criteria, the new scheme has been significantly optimized in terms of accuracy and processing speed for a variety of challenges, showing stronger performance superiority. Therefore, in the process of abnormal event monitoring and alarm optimization of power system, the simulation scheme based on the improved genetic algorithm successfully overcomes the shortcomings of the traditional improved particle swarm optimization and significantly improves the accuracy and operation efficiency of the simulation.

Author Keywords: Monitoring of abnormal events in the system

articleTitle: An IoT-Enabled Intelligent Real-Time Food Quality Monitoring System Using Low Cost Sensors
abstract: In order to create novel devices with applications in a number of technological domains, including the food business, it has been studied how multipurpose sensors have changed over the last few decades. Intelligent food packaging has been made possible by the incorporation of such sensors into food packaging technology. These integrated systems are able to offer trustworthy information regarding the caliber of the packaged goods throughout their storage time. To achieve this, intelligent packs make use of a range of sensors designed for tracking the evolution of variables like the number of disease agents, humidity, temperature, and storage period. These parameters include number of gases, temperature, pathogen agents, humidity, storage time. The electronic devices can supply much more data than traditional meals when integrated with IoT. Nowadays, nearly everyone is impacted by the food they eat. This goes beyond junk food; it is also including all packaged meals, veggies and everybody items that are ingested and utilized because they are all of poor quality due to fluctuations in temperature, moisture content, and oxygen content.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning-Based Pneumonia Detection System
abstract: Pneumonia ranks among the world's major causes of mortality and is the greatest cause of death for young children. It is an infectious condition that can be fatal, affects one or both lungs and is brought on by harmful bacteria. An accurate and timely diagnosis is essential for managing and treating patients effectively. Radiotherapists with specialized training are needed to assess chest X-rays to diagnose pneumonia. Therefore, creating an automated approach to identify pneumonia would be advantageous to treat the illness, especially in isolated locations quickly. This project offers a novel method for improving chest X-ray image quality, which is then used in conjunction with machine learning approaches to increase the detection accuracy of pneumonia. Subtle details in X-rays can be seen much better using picture-enhancing techniques including sharpening, contrast stretching, and histogram equalization. A VGG net and a convolutional neural network (CNN) model that can accurately diagnose pneumonia is trained using this augmented image dataset. By bridging the gap between conventional X-ray imaging and sophisticated machine learning, the initiative offers a viable approach to the early and accurate detection of pneumonia. Early disease identification is greatly aided by medical imaging, and chest X-rays are a frequent method of identifying lung disorders like pneumonia. This project offers a novel method for improving chest X-ray image quality, which is then used in conjunction with machine learning approaches to increase the detection accuracy of pneumonia. Subtle details in X-rays can be seen much better using picture-enhancing techniques including sharpening, contrast stretching, and histogram equalization. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model that can accurately diagnose pneumonia is trained using this augmented image dataset. By bridging the gap between conventional X-ray imaging and sophisticated machine learning, the initiative offers a viable approach to the early and accurate detection of pneumonia.

articleTitle: Enhanced Classification of Beech Bark Diseases Using CNN-MLP Fusion: A Multiclass Approach
abstract: Beech tree skin illnesses are common dangers to forest systems, needing the right and fast sorting methods to check how bad stages matter most for full handling plans. This research brings in a smart mix of methods using the powers of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) to find out how bad beech bark diseases (BBD) are at different stages. Using a carefully picked set of 2000 very clear images, that show many different and hard-to-understand disease signs; this study looks deep into the careful sorting out of these levels of being serious. The model's great work is outstanding, with a really good overall rightness of 94.47% over five clear-cut levels of seriousness. Tough measuring tools, including accuracy, remembering and F1-score keep proving the model is good at exactly putting complicated differences in disease stages. The clear accuracy of the model shows it can pick up small details found in these steps. This points to how important it could be when dealing with tree care and also sickness control. These results show hopeful ideas for checking illnesses, finding them early, and knowing how best to help affected forest areas with the hard problems of BBD.

articleTitle: A MI and DenseNet Based Feature Selection and Classification of Gene Expression Data
abstract: Introducing a groundbreaking approach, the paper unveils MI_DenseNet, a cancer classification procedure that employs mutual information and deep learning to achieve precise classification. The method involves preprocessing the data, converting it into 2D images, and utilizing a DenseNet model for classification. The experimental results demonstrate that MI_DenseNet outperforms another type of classification methods, showcasing best result. This study dives deep into the world of cancer analysis, where researchers mine data across different cancer types to unlock secrets hidden within. It emphasizes the crucial role of accurate early-stage cancer detection and prediction, not just for individual patients but for shaping the future of cancer research.

articleTitle: Sophisticated Weapon Detection Algorithms: A Quintuple Class Approach Using CNN-SVM
abstract: To obtain a metric precision of 88.33% and a metric recall of 87.13%, the Fl-Score being 87.72%. The data shows three classes separated as Class 1, which occupies 20% of the dataset (1903 cases) out of 9462 cases in the set. For Class 1, we produced an effect of 95%. As a Class 2, its precision reached 88.71 % with a recall value of 93.17% and an F1 score of 90.88%, where 1830 cases with 19% coverage of the dataset were considered, and overall accuracy achieved 96%. The performance is marked by an accuracy rate of 89.98%, a recall rate of 89.1 %, and an Fl-Score of 89.54. This group saw the count of 1935, which is a fifth of all data set. Briefly, the Class 3 precision is 96%. The class 4 precision level stands at 90.03%, the recall level is 92.61 %, and the Fl-Score is 91.3%, with 1881 cases corresponding to 20% of the data set and the eventual model accuracy at 97%. Class 5 stands for its specificity regarding the high marks achieved. The accuracy is 94.4%, the recall is 89.57%, and the Fl-Score is 91.92%. Moreover, not only is it the most common one with 1975 occurrences that constitute 21 % percent of the file, but it also has the most extensive support out of all the words. Lastly, it meets a record accuracy of 97%. The paper, which leans on macro, micro, and weighted averages, depicts the general output of the model. The macro means accuracy, recall, and Fl-Score are approximately 0.902940395, 0.903121043, and 0.902721029. This said, the model is uniformly triumphant in each category.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Various Slot in Patch Antennas: A Review
abstract: In the ever-evolving landscape of wireless communication, the demand for compact, high-performance antennas spanning a broad frequency range has become paramount. Microstrip patch antennas have emerged as a promising solution for fulfilling this demand, offering versatility and adaptability in various configurations. This research delves into a comparative analysis of different microstrip patch antenna designs tailored for broadband applications in the 2.4-6 GHz frequency range. As wireless technologies continue to advance, understanding the nuances of antenna performance becomes pivotal in achieving optimal communication systems. By scrutinizing the characteristics of E-shaped, U-shaped, Hexagonal, Circular, H-slot, Octagonal, and Rectangular microstrip patch antennas, this study aims to provide valuable insights that will inform the selection and design process for future wireless communication applications. The investigation spans crucial parameters such as bandwidth, gain, radiation pattern, return loss, impedance matching, and antenna efficiency, aiming to distill practical considerations for engineers and researchers working on the forefront of electronics and communication engineering.

articleTitle: FASAL FUSION: An Approach to Transform Crop Recommendations
abstract: In today's world of technology, farmers in several parts of India still face crop production problems due to soil and climate. No guide is available to assist them in choosing the appropriate types of plants that should be grown. The elevated suicide rate among Indian farmers, with 154 daily cases, is largely driven by “family problems” and “illness,” as reported in the 2022 NCRB annual study [1]. In this paper, a Crop Recommendation System that recommends a crop which is best suited for the soil by keeping Nitrogen (N), Phosphorus (P), Potassium (K), Humidity, Rainfall, Temperature, and pH as the main factors is proposed. It is a combination of a robust system for soil analysis, optimization and recommendation algorithms, to recommend crops. This approach has the potential to significantly improve the accuracy and efficiency of soil quality assessment and nutrient analysis. It can assist farmers in making informed crop choices, optimizing resource utilization, and enhancing overall agricultural productivity. The user inputs the values of N, P, K, humidity, rainfall, temperature, and pH, based on these values the selected Machine Learning algorithms have been used for the best crop prediction. The Random Forest Algorithm gives us the best results with 99.24% accuracy among Decision Tree Classifier (DTC), K-Nearest Neighbour Algorithm (KNN), Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine Algorithm (SVM), Logistic Regression Algorithm (LR), and AdaBoost Algorithm.

articleTitle: Coronary Artery Disease Detection in Early Stages Using Machine Learning
abstract: Cardiovascular disease presents a formidable healthcare challenge globally, necessitating substantial resources for treatments and surgeries. Timely detection and prediction are imperative for effective interventions. This study explores the potential of machine learning techniques, including artificial neural networks (ANN), decision trees (DT), random forests (RF), support vector machines (SVM), naïve Bayes (NB), and k-nearest neighbor algorithms, in predicting heart disease using healthcare data. The increasing prevalence of premature coronary artery disease (PCAD) has spurred investigations into its occurrence and predisposing factors. In India, cardiovascular diseases (CVD) reign as the primary cause of mortality and disability, marked by heightened risks, earlier onset, and amplified fatality rates. Researchers attribute this burden to population-level shifts and intrinsic biological risks influenced by diverse life stages. While conventional risk factors elucidate a substantial portion of the risk, these factors exhibit distinct thresholds in Indian populations. Prenatal and postnatal factors, inherent metabolic disparities, inflammation, genetics, and epigenetics all play pivotal roles. A comprehensive approach, considering both population-level dynamics and biological factors, is indispensable to mitigate the escalating CVD epidemic among diverse populations.

articleTitle: Exploring the Causal Dynamics of Covariates on Emotional Responses: Implications for Psychology and Human-Computer Interaction
abstract: The causal dynamics of covariates of emotional responses and EEG brain wave signals offer implications for psychology, user experience design, and human-computer interaction. With advances in brain-machine interaction, machine learning, and emotion analysis, the study employs a comprehensive framework that combines linear regression and structural equation modelling to identify key covariates that influence emotional valence and arousal, fundamental dimensions of emotions. This research study uses Dataset for Emotion Analysis using Physiological Signals (DEAP) with EEG recordings, time-stamped observations, and emotional labels. The results show a robust causal relationship between EEG wave recordings and emotional valence with varying accuracy in predicting arousal. The Instrumentation Variable (IV) Estimation values provide causal dynamics of EEG brain waves with Valence and Arousal using adjusted R-squared values, log-likelihood and Information Criteria (MAE(0.02 to 0.19), adjusted R-Squared(0.21 to 0.91), negative AIC/BIC scores(> -153800.00)) The results contribute to the understanding of the complex interplay between neural activity patterns and emotional states, with implications for refining psychological interventions, optimizing user experiences, and promoting symbiotic human-computer interactions.

articleTitle: Kannada Character Recognition Using Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: India is a country with many states, the form of documentation in Government offices and healthcare departments are in regional languages, and digitizing the document is a challenge. Thus, the current study focuses on Kannada (a regional language in Karnataka state, India) handwritten character identification approach uses techniques of image pre-processing techniques to improve image quality and deep learning approaches for feature extraction and thereby classification of Kannada characters. The Chars74K dataset was utilized to train the network. The trained model is capable of classifying handwritten Kannada vowels and consonants. In comparison to other architectures, MobileN etV2 has demonstrated high performance.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review and Analysis of Landslide Detection Through Advanced Image Analysis Techniques
abstract: Landslides are among the most destructive natural hazards, causing substantial loss of life and property damage worldwide. Remote sensing through satellite imagery has emerged as a valuable tool for studying and monitoring landslides over large areas. This review paper provides a systematic examination of the application of satellite data and image processing techniques for landslide detection and mapping. The literature review conducted across major scientific databases yielded over 500 initial results, of which 35 papers were selected for final review based on relevance, rigor, and innovation. The review summarizes key trends, datasets, methods, and challenges related to landslide detection using optical, radar, and LiDAR data. Analysis reveals that integration of multiple sensors, use of machine learning algorithms, and object-based image analysis have significantly improved landslide detection accuracy. However, challenges remain in distinguishing landslide signals from noise, handling data gaps, and transferring models across different geographical settings. Satellite-based landslide detection has immense potential for hazard assessment and disaster response if current limitations can be addressed through multi-temporal analysis, model generalization, and combination with ground data. This review provides a synthesis of current research and identifies promising directions for future work toward an operational landslide detection system using satellite imagery.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Heart Disease Prediction Using ECG Image
abstract: In a global health context outlined by the World Health Organization (WHO), the escalating prevalence of CVDs underscores a pressing need for advanced diagnostic methodologies. CVDs remain a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, necessitating innovative approaches for early detection. Traditional diagnostic methods face challenges in providing timely and accurate identification of heart conditions, often relying on subjective interpretation and lacking the sensitivity required for early intervention. Recognizing this critical gap, our engineering project focuses on the early detection of heart diseases using ML and DL techniques applied to ECG images. The integration of ML and DL offers a promising avenue to overcome the limitations of conventional diagnostic tools, leveraging intricate patterns within ECG data for more precise and timely detection. By addressing these challenges, our research aims to contribute to the advancement of cardiovascular health, providing a robust framework for early disease detection and improving overall patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Enhancing Urban Home Security: Deep Learning Enabled Vehicle Identification
abstract: The growing rate of crimes in cities is a genuine concern these days. Preventing crimes from happening is a need for the city residents and the administrator community. Various technology-enabled solution approaches can be integrated to prevent crimes in cities. In this work, we explore how the amalgamation of Deep Learning and IoT can prevent crimes and provide enhanced security to citizens. Crimes happen for several reasons, and the right technology-enabled solutions can help prevent crimes by alerting the intended stakeholders on time. This paper focuses on the importance of identifying vehicles and the importance of detecting non-resident vehicles to alert the residents and related security personnel about them. We detailed the steps used to identify the vehicle using YOLOv8. The work also explored various OCR tools to find the best one for number plate identification.

articleTitle: Automated Gastrointestinal Tract Image Segmentation
abstract: The number of people acquiring a gastrointestinal (GI) cancer diagnosis is increasing annually. In the realm of biomedicine, radiation treatment is the accepted gold standard for treating gastrointestinal cancer. An X-ray beam is directed towards the tumour during radiation therapy, sparing the nearby healthy tissue. For an oncologist, manually segmenting healthy organs can be laborious and prone to mistakes. Thus, there is a need for technology that can autonomously segregate the healthy organs of the GI tract. In response to this demand, our work suggests an innovative approach that uses ensemble learning to enhance model performance. Two different deep-learning architectures are used to create the ensemble: the DenseNet and InceptionResNetv2 models. The main goal is to identify healthy organs inside the GI tract and offer a more reliable and efficient segmentation method than manual segmentation, ultimately contributing to more effective radiation therapy treatments for patients diagnosed with GI cancer. Radio oncologists can greatly accelerate the treatment process and provide faster, more precise treatments by utilizing an automated system. By utilizing the GI Tract Image Segmentation dataset from UW-Madison, the suggested approach was implemented, guaranteeing a solid basis for training and testing. By combining the benefits of both InceptionResNetv2 and DenseNet201, ensemble learning seeks to provide a model that is more reliable and accurate for the given job. The key strengths of this approach lie in its robustness, scalability, and computational efficiency. The model attained a commendable Dice coefficient of 0.89, indicating a high level of accuracy in organ segmentation. This indicates the possibility for a smooth integration of the suggested deep learning-based solution into clinical processes in addition to proving its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of SMIS Data Security Based on Hybrid Encryption Algorithm and FUK Technology
abstract: In order to solve the challenges of SMIS data security design and implementation, in view of the shortcomings of the existing LSH algorithms, this study introduces an innovative SMIS data security design and implementation method based on hybrid encryption algorithm and FUK technology. This new scheme uses the principles of asymmetric cryptography theory to accurately identify and locate key influencing factors, and accordingly performs a sensible classification of indicators to reduce possible interference. At the same time, using the unique mechanism of hybrid encryption algorithm and FUK technology, the design strategy of security design is cleverly constructed. The empirical results show that the proposed scheme shows significant improvement compared with the traditional LSH algorithm in key performance indicators such as the accuracy of SMIS data security design and implementation, and the processing efficiency of key factors, showing its obvious strong advantages. SMIS data security design and implementation plays a vital role in intelligent big data, which can accurately predict and optimize the growth trend and output results of SMIS data security design and implementation. However, in the face of complex simulation tasks, traditional LSH algorithms show some inherent shortcomings, especially when dealing with multilevel challenges, their performance is often unsatisfactory. To overcome this problem, this study introduces a new idea of SMIS data security design and implementation optimized by hybrid encryption algorithm and FUK technology, and accurately controls the influencing parameters through asymmetric encryption theory, and uses this as a road map for index allocation, and then uses hybrid encryption algorithm and FUK technology innovation to construct a system scheme. The test results clearly point out that in the context of the evaluation criteria, the new scheme has been significantly optimized in terms of accuracy and processing speed for a variety of challenges, showing stronger performance superiority. Therefore, in the design and implementation of SMIS data security, the simulation scheme based on hybrid encryption algorithm and FUK technology successfully overcomes the shortcomings of the traditional LSH algorithm and significantly improves the accuracy and operation efficiency of the simulation.

Author Keywords: asymmetric cryptography theory;Hybrid encryption algorithm with FUK technology;Intelligent Big Data;Safety by design;Implementation

articleTitle: Predicting Job Opportunities Through Twitter Data Using Natural Language Processing
abstract: The research illuminates the intriguing potential of applying Natural Language Processing (NLP) methodologies to scrutinize Twitter API, construct predictive performance models, pinpoint nascent corporations, and acquire an understanding of the employment market panorama. By capitalizing on data analytics and machine learning, the objective is to formulate proficient models capable of distilling meaningful insights from a wide array of tweets, thereby revealing potential business opportunities. The article intends to illustrate how the amalgamation of NLP, data analytics, and machine learning can be employed to exploit the capabilities of Twitter data in forecasting job opportunities and offering valuable intelligence for businesses navigating in a dynamic and swiftly evolving marketplace.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis of Unified Payments Interface (UPI) Payment App Review using Machine Learning Algorithm
abstract: The paper “Sentiment Analysis of UPI Application Reviews using Machine Learning Algorithm” uses natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning to analyse user evaluations of Unified Payments Interface (UPI) applications for sentiments. The objective is to conduct a comparative analysis of different algorithms to better understand the user reviews of UPI applications and provide useful data for these digital platforms' strategic enhancements. Preprocessing is done on datasets, which includes text transformation with techniques like Word2Vec and Bag of Words. These techniques transform raw text into numerical vectors that are used by machine learning algorithms. Reviews are categorised into positive and negative sentiments using sentiment analysis algorithms. For sentiment classification, algorithms like C 4.5 (J48), Naive Bayes, and LSTM are used. Their effectiveness is assessed through comparative analysis. 90.02% was the highest accuracy recorded for sentiment classification of user reviews on Paytm. LSTM in conjunction with the word2vec skip-gram training model resulted in the attainment of this prediction. Results provide perceptions into user sentiments, facilitating purposeful enhancements in UPI applications that boost user contentment and adhere to changing digital payment requirements.

articleTitle: Multi-Class Urban Sound Classification with Deep Learning Architectures
abstract: In the area of urban sound classification, our re-search delves into the challenge of correctly categorizing diverse urban soundscapes. Employing deep learning models like Arti-ficial neural networks (ANNs), Convolutional neural networks (CNNs), Recurrent neural networks (RNNs), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, we aim to decode complex patterns within audio data for optimal classification. Utilizing Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCCs) for feature extraction, we explore the strengths and trade-offs of each architecture. Our study not only advances urban sound classification but also emphasizes the advantages and considerations of each model, providing practical insights for real-world applications in urban audio analysis. The Artificial Neural Network (ANN) showcases an impressive accuracy of 94.79 %, emphasizing its robust per-formance in capturing key sound features. Following closely, the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) achieves a notable accuracy of 93.64 %, highlighting its proficiency in spatial feature extraction. The Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) achieves an accuracy of 65.14%, offering insights into its suitability for specific sound classification tasks. Additionally, the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) architecture emerges as a significant contributor with an accuracy of 86.09 %, underlining its effective-ness in capturing complex temporal dependencies. These results highlight the diverse strengths of each architecture and LSTM in particular performs exceptionally well in classifying urban sounds, which enhances the possibility of practical applications in this field.

articleTitle: Hybridized Model for Improved Papaya Leaf Disease Classification: CNN and Random Forest Integration
abstract: The main goal of the study is to find a way to group things into categories that can be used to find diseases in papaya leaves. To reach this objective, this framework will be planned and checked in line with the requirements. Plants can be put into the following six groups so the model can properly sort them: “Healthy,” “Papaya Ringspot Virus (PRSV),” “Papaya Leaf Curl Virus (PLCV),” “Powdery Mildew,” “Papaya Mosaic Virus (PapMV),” and “Leaf Spot Diseases.” Random Forest along with Convolutional Neural Networks, or CNN for short, are both used together by the model at the same time. Several variables, including accuracy, recall, and F1-score, are used to measure how well the model can tell the difference between these groups. The model has accuracy rates that range from 94.44% to 96.22%, which shows that it can correctly identify a wide range of illnesses, as the results show. This shows that the system can give accurate positive predictions. The remembering rates run from 94.12% to 96.13%, which also shows that the model can correctly tell the difference between events that involve each illness. These things are clear because this model works well. The F1 scores, which add up to an average of 95.48%, show that tasks have been consistently completed. In this study, the results show that there is a mix of accuracy and memory. The model has also gotten a total value of 95.49%, which shows how well it can find diseases that show up on papaya leaves right now. This number includes both good and bad results. The system seems to be accurate and useful for finding diseases based on the results of these tests. This means that the technology might be able to be used in real farming situations.

articleTitle: Systolic Digital IIR Filter Architectures for Real Time Signal Processing Applications
abstract: Digital Signal Processing (DSP) is a critical area of research within Very Large-Scale Integration (VLSI) due to its vital role in various applications such as telecommunications, multimedia, radar, and medical imaging. DSP is essential for achieving real-time performance, low power consumption, and optimized hardware implementations. As VLSI technologies advance to support emerging fields like AI, IoT, and edge computing, DSP remains essential, driving innovations in algorithms and architectures to meet the demands of these rapidly advancing technologies. Here we are using different Architectures for reducing usage of power, delay and PDP and also to find efficiency Quality Metrics is provided.

articleTitle: MRI Scans for Deep Learning-Based Chronic Nephropathy Detection: A Comparison of CNN, MobileNet, VGG16, and ResNet-50 Models
abstract: Prolonged Nephropathy Given that detection usually shows no signs in its early phases and has a high morbidity rate, it presents a serious danger to world health. This research paper proposes a machine learning architecture that uses models based on deep learning (CNN, MobileNet, VGG16, ResNet-50) to identify illness using MRI data. 12,446 images in the dataset obtained through Kaggle are categorized as normal, cyst, stone, and malignancy. The study evaluates the models' performances, and ResNet-50 exhibits the highest accuracy. The VGG16 and ResNet-50 designs for the proposed system are presented, with a focus on their characteristics. Pre-processing, instruction, classification, and collection of data are all included in the implementation. Users may upload their photos to be classified by different algorithms. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the ResNet-50 model, which had an overall 98% classification accuracy for renal diseases. In conclusion, the application of deep learning specifically, the ResNet-50 model shows promise as a quick and dependable technique for detection, therefore alleviating a major healthcare issue.

articleTitle: Addressing Class Imbalance for Improved Pneumonia Diagnosis: Comparative Analysis of GANs and Weighted Loss Function in Classification of the Chest X-Ray Images
abstract: Pneumonia detection using the chest X-ray images is genuinely, a critical task in the medical field of study and research, still there are multiple prevailing challenges, that include the overfitting and the lack of generalization in the existing models, because of scarcity in data and class imbalance. In response, the study on the problem statement introduces a comparative analysis that aims at significant enhancement of accuracy in pneumonia diagnosis. Our approach highlights on evaluating the effectiveness of two distinct methodologies: a weighted loss function and Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs).
